accuracy_findings.claim: Population counts with its fraction, so a system just below a threshold stays in the class under it.

clarity_findings.problem: The page invents the phrase "system points" as its running term for this stat, but that is not the game's own name for it. The real UI-facing label, `data.victory.population.points` in front/src/locales/en/data.json, is "Star System Points" (surfaced via a `{name:}` token). The page never uses that name — instead it says "worth a number of system points" in the defining sentence, claims `system points` in its own `terms:` list, repeats "system points" four more times in the body, and then separately quotes the generated table's column header as "Victory points" (a third, different spelling, hardcoded in lib/rc/help/format.ex:31) — so the same value is named three different ways on one page, none of which is the literal name shown in-game.
clarity_findings.failure_scenario: A player who has seen the real tooltip/stat label "Star System Points" in the game reads this page calling it "system points", sees the table column say "Victory points", and cannot tell whether these are the same number or three related-but-different things.
clarity_findings.quote: A population class is the size tier of a system, set by its population and worth a number of system points.
clarity_findings.fix: Replace the free-hand "system points" throughout the prose (and in `terms:`) with the `{name:victory.population.points}` token (renders "Star System Points"), so the page's own vocabulary matches what the game actually shows the player.

clarity_findings.problem: "Victory points" (the table column, and the word used in the final paragraph) and "system points" (the term used everywhere else) are used as if interchangeable, but the final paragraph's "victory points" actually refers to a different, higher-level quantity — the whole faction's win-condition score (compared against a win target, e.g. `leader.victory_points >= win_target` in lib/game/instance/victory/victory.ex) — not the per-system value the rest of the page is about. The page never signals that these are different things.
clarity_findings.failure_scenario: A reader finishes the page believing that a system's own "points" (shown in its tooltip) are directly the same currency counted toward the game's overall win condition, when the text is actually describing two different scores (a per-path standing vs. the win-total currency) using the same words.
clarity_findings.quote: System points are not added to the win total. The path earns victory points only when the sum reaches a milestone.
clarity_findings.fix: Use two visibly distinct terms — e.g. keep the per-system value as {name:victory.population.points} ("Star System Points") and refer to the win-condition currency plainly as something like "the faction's overall victory-point total" — so the two concepts never share a bare word.

clarity_findings.problem: The closing paragraph introduces three new proper nouns back-to-back — "Path of Influence", the "Road to Victory panel", and "the win total" / "a milestone" — none of which are defined, and none of which can be linked because no victory-system page exists yet (victory/ranking is a different, later category per docs/help-manual.md §5.2 category 9). A first-time reader has no way to know what any of these three things are or how they relate to each other or to the population-class page they're reading.
clarity_findings.failure_scenario: A new player reads "shown in the Road to Victory panel" and "the path earns victory points only when the sum reaches a milestone" and comes away with three unexplained UI names and no idea what a "milestone" is or how many there are.
clarity_findings.quote: That sum is the faction's Path of Influence score, shown in the Road to Victory panel. System points are not added to the win total. The path earns victory points only when the sum reaches a milestone.
clarity_findings.fix: Trim this paragraph to the one fact that belongs on a population-class page — that a system's points feed into the faction's population-path standing — and drop the win-total/milestone detail entirely until a victory-system page exists to carry (and link) it.

clarity_findings.problem: "Population counts with its fraction" is opaque on a first read — a reader has to reach the worked example two lines later to reverse-engineer that this means population is compared to the threshold including its decimal part (so 89.9 stays below the 90-threshold class).
clarity_findings.failure_scenario: A reader stops at this sentence, re-reads it, and still isn't sure what "counts with its fraction" is contrasting against (rounding? truncation?) until the example below spells it out.
clarity_findings.quote: Population counts with its fraction, so a system just below a threshold stays in the class under it.
clarity_findings.fix: State the comparison directly, e.g. "A system's population is compared to each threshold including its decimal part, so a population of 89.9 is still below the 90 threshold."

clarity_findings.problem: "Visibility" is used twice with a bare numeric cutoff ("below 3", "3 or higher") but is never defined on this page, and the one page it could point to ([[map-legend]]) only names a "visibility mode" without explaining what the 0-4-ish scale means or where a level comes from.

clarity_findings.quote: A system's population is compared to each threshold including its decimal part, so a population of 89.9 is still below the 90 threshold.
clarity_findings.problem: The threshold value 90 is hard-coded into flowing prose, not marked as an example and not a {const:} token — yet 90 is a content-table value (the "Major System" class threshold from population_classes), already shown correctly in the indented Example block right below ("population 90.0 -> class starting at 90, 16 points"). If that threshold is ever rebalanced, this sentence goes stale independently of the table/example, which is exactly what the numbers rule (every number that exists in code/content is a token or lives in a generated table) is meant to prevent.
clarity_findings.fix: Drop the specific numbers from the topic sentence and let the existing Example block carry them, e.g.: "A system's population is compared to each threshold including its decimal part, so a population just under a threshold still counts toward the lower class." The two Example lines already demonstrate this with real, run-derived numbers.

clarity_findings.quote: Each class is worth a number of points, which the galaxy map calls {ui:panel.help.legend_mode_population_name}.
clarity_findings.problem: This is the first mention of the galaxy map's points display, and it carries no link. The page's only [[map-legend]] link is attached to the *second* mention of the same feature, later in "Where it shows" ("The galaxy map's ... mode shows the points only on systems at visibility 3 or higher; see [[map-legend]]"). Rule 7 requires the link at first appearance.
clarity_findings.fix: Move (or add) the link to the first mention, e.g.: "...which the galaxy map ([[map-legend]]) calls {ui:panel.help.legend_mode_population_name}." and drop the now-redundant "see [[map-legend]]" tag from the later sentence, or keep both if the second is a distinct enough reference.

clarity_findings.quote: The table's last column lists each class's {ui:panel.help.legend_mode_population_name}. ... The sum is the faction's standing on the {name:victory.population}. The {ui:minipanel.victory.title} panel shows it under "Star System Points".
clarity_findings.problem: The page names the same underlying quantity three different ways with no statement that they're the same thing: the body calls it "System points" (map-legend UI label) throughout, but the table's actual last column is literally headed "Victory points" (lib/rc/help/tables.ex renders `t(ctx, :victory_points)` for population_classes — never "System points"), and the closing sentence quotes yet a third label, "Star System Points" (the victory mini-panel). A first-time reader looking at the table will see a column called "Victory points" right after being told the table shows "System points," and then meet "Star System Points" with no link between the three. Each label is a real UI string (rule 3 is satisfied), but nothing ties them together, so the page reads as if there might be three related-but-different stats.
clarity_findings.fix: Add one short clause the first time each new label appears, e.g. after introducing the table: "(labeled Victory points in the table below)", and before the closing quote: "...same points, which the {ui:minipanel.victory.title} panel shows under 'Star System Points'."

clarity_findings.quote: A system's population is compared to each threshold including its decimal part, so a population of 89.9 is still below the 90 threshold.
clarity_findings.problem: Needs a second read: "including its decimal part" sits awkwardly between "population" and "is compared," so on first pass it can look like the decimal part is what's being compared, rather than the sentence saying comparisons are exact/fractional-inclusive.
clarity_findings.fix: Reorder for a single pass, e.g.: "A system's population is compared to each threshold down to the decimal — a population of 89.9 is still below the 90 threshold."

clarity_findings.quote: The sum is the faction's standing on the {name:victory.population}.
clarity_findings.problem: Resolves to "the Path of Influence" with zero context. Since no victory/victory-points page exists yet to link to, the name lands as an unexplained proper noun — a reader has no way to know this is one of several victory tracks rather than a one-off label.
clarity_findings.fix: Add a short appositive so the term is at least placed, without over-explaining out-of-scope victory mechanics: "...the faction's standing on the Path of Influence, one of the game's victory tracks."

clarity_findings.quote: In the system view, a system's {ui:panel.help.legend_mode_population_name} show as a number next to the owner name. Its tooltip names the class...
clarity_findings.problem: "Its" has an ambiguous antecedent on first read — it could point to "System points," "a number," or "a system"; the intended referent (the displayed number's tooltip) only becomes clear after re-reading.
clarity_findings.fix: Replace the pronoun: "...show as a number next to the owner name. That number's tooltip names the class..."
